The Chief Research Scientist and Director at the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research–Crops Research Institute (CSIR-CRI), Professor Maxwell Darko Asante, says Ghanaian farmers are losing confidence in rice farming due to difficulties in selling their produce.
He attributes the situation to the influx of cheaper imported rice, which he says has made it difficult for locally produced rice to compete in the domestic market.
According to him, repeated government assurances to purchase locally produced rice have yielded little or no results, leaving farmers with large quantities of unsold produce.
"So for the last couple of years, farmers, especially rice farmers, have suffered a lot because there are a lot of cheap imports and they are not able to sell their rice. So announcing a policy is not enough for them to go back to the field; even if they wish to go back to the field, there is no money for them to go back,"
"The confidence of the farmers has really been broken," he said on Joy FM's Super Morning Show on Tuesday, November 17.
Professor Asante said the situation has discouraged some farmers to the extent that they no longer want to invest in rice cultivation.
He cited an interaction with some rice farmers who openly told him they had lost interest in the business because the government had failed to purchase their produce, while imported varieties continued to dominate the market.
"We invited some farmers from one of the Brong areas to train in seed production. When they came, about 20 farmers told us that not a single one of them planted rice this year because they are not able to sell the previous year's harvest," he said.
"So it is very important that the government does that (purchase their rice) immediately to restore confidence in rice farming," he added.
He said the development poses a challenge to efforts to strengthen Ghana's domestic rice production, particularly at a time when the country is seeking to expand its industrial and agricultural capacity.
His comments come amid discussions about Ghana's production capacity following reports that Africa's richest man, Aliko Dangote, has expressed interest in investing in the country's proposed super factory.
